findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed run's declared write scope names docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/code-progress-totals.html and docs/figures/jt60sa-discovery-completion/code-progress-totals, but neither exists at the reviewed head aa5834427 (the fragment file is absent and no code-progress-totals figures directory was created; the diff base..head touches only three files). A declared write path that produced nothing reads as unfinished work or as a scope that over-states the run.

follow-on: the plan's deliverable says 'every query in get_code_discovery_stats is valid Cypher', but the capturing test asserts only that no query contains '{{' or '}}'. A different syntax error (an unbalanced paren, a misspelled clause) would pass. This matches the plan's own done-when wording ('asserts none contains a doubled brace'), so it is a narrowing of the deliverable, not a failure of the clause; a stronger check would parse each captured query with the Cypher parser or spellcheck the intended node/relationship names.

follow-on: the dedup key is (type(exc), str(exc)). An exception whose message embeds volatile content -- a file path, a row count, a timestamp, the facility name -- yields a new key on every refresh, so the 'once per distinct error' intent degrades to 'once per distinct message' and the warning can repeat every graph_refresh_interval. The set is also unbounded within a run, though the cardinality is trivial in practice. No test exercises a message with variable content.

follow-on: evidence hygiene in the reviewed artifact, not a code defect. The reviewed manifest's baseline_suite object is empty, so a reader deriving added failures from the run's own evidence gets a head arm only and cannot compute a delta; the comparable base arm was supplied by this review (base 2 failed -> head 0 failed). Its baseline-query.log is also a partial baseline: it collected one test (the logging test did not yet exist), so it is not a full-file base arm.

justifications.durability: both guards are controls rather than assertions of intent, demonstrated by mutation. The brace guard fails when the doubled brace is restored (reproduced), and the logging guard fails when the swallow is restored (base arm: warnings == []). The dedup state is a per-invocation local set, so a fresh run re-warns, which matches 'once per distinct error'. Residual risk is finding 3: the dedup key is (type(exc), str(exc)), so an error whose message embeds volatile content (a path, a count, a timestamp) will be logged on every refresh rather than once, and no test covers that shape.
justifications.evidence: an independent base arm (2 failed, EXIT=1) and head arm (2 passed, EXIT=0) close the added-failure question at zero, and the declared negative control is reproduced (1 failed / 1 passed, EXIT=1). The two failures at base are genuine fail->pass transitions: at base the braces test fails on the first query and the refresh test fails with an empty warning list, so both new tests are load-bearing. Gaps: the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite is empty, so the run's own evidence gives no base arm (finding 4); and the run's baseline-query.log header names revision 21c117291 while collecting only the one test that existed then, before the logging test was added.
justifications.fit: the change is minimal and idiomatic: it uses the module logger already present, keeps the loop's existing CancelledError re-raise ordering, and adds no new abstraction. Commits carry conventional subjects with bodies, and neither the messages, the test file, nor the comments carry plan, sprint, ticket, PR or author identifiers (checked). Tests are named by mechanism.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the plan's cause is reproduced at base and refuted at head. At base the first query string contains a literal '{{id: $facility}}' (AssertionError: assert '{{' not in '...'), and the refresh loop's 'except Exception: pass' produces an empty warning list; at head the query is valid and the two distinct errors are each logged once. All three done-when clauses (capturing test, logging test, negative control) hold and were independently reproduced. Slight reserve: the deliverable word 'valid Cypher' is stronger than the test, which checks only brace doubling (finding 2).
justifications.reuse: nothing is re-implemented: the refresh loop's structure, the logger, and the display teardown are unchanged, and the test drives the real run_discovery path with unittest.mock patches rather than a shadow harness. It introduces no parallel helper for query capture because none exists in the repo. The brace fix aligns the first query with the seven sibling query strings in the same function.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff stays inside the declared product write scope across both commits (parallel.py, common.py, the new test file) and introduces no unrelated edit; it touches no docs, no plan, and no index. The reserve is that the declared write scope also names docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/code-progress-totals.html and docs/figures/jt60sa-discovery-completion/code-progress-totals, neither of which exists at the reviewed head (finding 1), so the declared scope over-states what the run touched rather than the work exceeding it.

raw_text: Review of r-20261008T222414302255-code-progress-totals against plan section 59 (jt60sa-discovery-completion). The reviewed diff fixes the first query in get_code_discovery_stats (a non-f plain string with a literal doubled brace that Neo4j rejects) and replaces the refresh loop's silent 'except Exception: pass' with a dedup-and-warn block, plus two tests. I reproduced the head gate (2 passed, EXIT=0), the base defect (2 failed, EXIT=1) and the declared negative control (1 failed / 1 passed, EXIT=1) in independent scratch arms under $TMPDIR; both new tests are genuine fail->pass transitions and the change adds no failing test. An AST scan for the same doubled-brace class in non-f-string literals found only legitimate .format() templates (standard_names/coverage.py) besides the now-fixed site, so no sibling defect is outstanding. Verdict: SOUND WITH FINDINGS.
